heard: Every star in the universe will eventually go out forever. All interstellar gas will run dry in about a hundred trillion years. The last remaining red dwarfs will slowly fade into dark black dwarfs. Gravitational encounters will then fling most dead stars into deep space. Only supermassive black holes will remain in the empty void. Yet even black holes lose mass. Through quantum Hawking radiation, the very last black holes will evaporate after one Google years. That leaves behind a frozen cosmos where no new light can ever ignite.
